title: MONID HABITRACK Cohort Study: A representative study for tick-borne encephalitis virus and Borrelia burgdorferi in Amberg-Sulzbach and Schwandorf
summary:
Tick-borne encephalitis (TBE) and Lyme borreliosis (Lyme disease) are the most common tick-borne diseases in Germany. Both are primarily transmitted by ticks of the species Ixodes ricinus, but differ in their causative pathogens and clinical courses. Lyme borreliosis is caused by bacteria and can affect the skin, nervous system and joints. Infections are often asymptomatic but may also cause symptoms such as erythema migrans (a characteristic expanding skin rash), neurological symptoms or joint inflammation. The disease can usually be treated with antibiotics. However, no vaccine is currently available in Germany. TBE is caused by a virus and is also frequently asymptomatic. In some infected individuals, the central nervous system may be affected, potentially resulting in long-term neurological symptoms. There is no specific treatment for TBE, however, vaccination provides effective protection.

The aim of this study is to investigate the prevalence of antibodies against TBE virus and Borrelia burgdorferi in the population of the districts of Amberg-Sulzbach and Schwandorf. The data collected will help identify areas with an increased risk of infection (so-called "hotspots") and investigate additional factors associated with infection risk.

Participants will be followed over a period of approximately two years, with repeated assessments to monitor changes over time. In total, participants will be asked to provide a blood sample and to complete a digital questionnaire at three different time points: in spring 2027 before the tick season and following the tick seasons at the end of 2027 and the end of 2028.

interventions.name: Participants will receive a test kit for self-collection of a capillary blood sample in total three times between 2027 and 2028. The blood samples will be sent back to the study centre by the study participants for laboratory analysis.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Primary residence in the districts of Amberg-Sulzbach or Schwandorf
and completion of an informed consent form (ICF)
Exclusion criteria:
Insufficient command of the German language to a degree that impedes
informed consent
